(CNN) — Leading jockey Frankie Dettori may have spent much of his life on a diet, but when it comes to his favorite pastimes, food ranks right alongside racing.

Around five years ago, Dettori met Michelin-starred chef Marco Pierre White and asked where he could take his young family out to eat.

“I couldn’t answer the question,” Marco Pierre White told CNN, “and that’s how Frankie’s was born. That simple.”

The pair opened their first restaurant in London in 2004. Today, there are four in London, one in Shanghai, and one in Dubai. This March, a cookbook followed: *Frankie Dettori’s Italian Family Cookbook*.

Below is Dettori’s favorite recipe. Enjoy.

Frankie: “My father loved this particular dish as, although it’s vegetarian, it has the meaty and slightly smoky texture of a good steak. To this day, it makes me think of childhood Sunday lunches.”

## Parmigiana di Melanzane / Aubergine Parmigiana

### Ingredients

- 1 kg aubergines  
- Extra virgin olive oil  
- Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper  
- 2 garlic cloves, chopped  
- 3 x 400g cans of good-quality tinned tomatoes, sieved and chopped  
- A small handful of fresh basil leaves  
- A large handful of finely grated Parmesan  
- 1½ kg fresh Mozzarella, cubed  

Preheat the oven to 180°C/350°F/Gas Mark 4.

Cut the aubergines lengthwise into ½cm strips. Sprinkle each slice with salt and layer them on a plate. Cover with a plate of the same size and place a heavy weight on top, such as a large bottle of water, to press the water out of the aubergines. Set aside for 2–3 hours.

Meanwhile, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a saucepan. Add the garlic and fry until slightly golden. Add the tomatoes and basil, then cook over a medium heat for 25 minutes, until the sauce thickens. Season to taste.

Remove the weight from the aubergines, rinse the slices thoroughly, and pat them dry. Generously cover the bottom of a large frying pan with olive oil and place over a high heat. Working in batches, brown the aubergine slices on both sides, lowering the heat and adding more oil as required. Drain the slices on kitchen roll as you go.

Cover the bottom of a 23cm x 30cm ovenproof dish with a thin layer of tomato sauce. Add a layer of aubergine slices, then top with a handful of the cheeses. Ladle some tomato sauce over the top and continue layering, finishing with a layer of tomato sauce and a sprinkling of cheeses.

Bake for 15–20 minutes, until heated through and the Mozzarella has melted. Set aside for a few minutes to cool. Cut into squares and serve warm.

Serves 8  
Preparation time: 3 hours  
Cooking time: 50 minutes  

Courtesy: HarperCollins Publishers

# Frankie Dettori and Marco Pierre White bet on comfort, charisma and Italian classics in new restaurant partnership

When Frankie Dettori talks about food, the energy is familiar: quick, animated, theatrical — not unlike the flying dismount that made him one of horse racing’s most recognizable figures.

For decades, Dettori’s name has been synonymous with speed, instinct and the roar of the grandstand. Marco Pierre White, meanwhile, built his reputation in a different kind of arena: the white heat of the professional kitchen, where discipline, precision and personality can matter as much as technique.

Now the jockey and the chef have brought those worlds together in a restaurant partnership that leans into something both men understand well: hospitality as performance.

The collaboration pairs Dettori’s Italian heritage and public warmth with White’s long-standing flair for polished, accessible dining. Rather than chasing culinary fashion, the concept centers on the kind of food both men say people actually want to return to — generous plates, classic flavors and the feeling of being looked after.

For Dettori, the connection to Italian cooking is personal. Born in Milan into a racing family, he grew up around the rhythms of home cooking: tomato sauce simmering slowly, vegetables layered with cheese, pasta served without fuss, and meals that lasted longer than expected.

White’s role brings structure and restaurant craft to that nostalgia. Known as the first British chef to earn three Michelin stars, he has spent much of his later career translating fine-dining instincts into broader, more relaxed formats. In this partnership, the emphasis is less on culinary fireworks and more on confidence: crisp service, recognizable dishes and a menu built around comfort.

The appeal is easy to understand. Diners are increasingly drawn to restaurants that feel both special and familiar — places with celebrity sparkle, but also the reassurance of a good bowl of pasta, a properly cooked steak or a bubbling dish of baked aubergine.

And it is aubergine parmigiana — melanzane alla parmigiana — that Dettori often returns to when speaking about the Italian food of home. Rich but not heavy when done well, it is the kind of dish that rewards patience: sliced aubergines, tomato sauce, basil, mozzarella and Parmesan baked until molten and golden.

Below is a family-style version of Frankie’s favorite aubergine parmigiana, the sort of recipe that belongs at the center of the table.

---

## Frankie’s favorite aubergine parmigiana

### Serves  
4 to 6

### Ingredients

- 3 large aubergines  
- Salt, for drawing out moisture  
- Olive oil, for brushing or frying  
- 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil  
- 1 small onion, finely chopped  
- 2 garlic cloves, finely sliced  
- 2 x 400g cans chopped tomatoes, or passata  
- A small handful of fresh basil leaves, plus extra to finish  
- 250g mozzarella, torn or sliced  
- 80g Parmesan, finely grated  
- Freshly ground black pepper  
- Optional: a little dried oregano or a pinch of sugar, depending on the tomatoes  

### Method

1. **Prepare the aubergines**  
   Slice the aubergines lengthways into pieces about 1cm thick. Sprinkle lightly with salt and leave in a colander for 30 minutes. Rinse briefly and pat dry with kitchen paper.

2. **Cook the aubergines**  
   Brush the slices with olive oil and grill, roast or pan-fry until soft and lightly golden on both sides. Set aside.  
   *Tip: Roasting is easier and lighter; frying gives a richer, more traditional result.*

3. **Make the tomato sauce**  
   Heat the extra-virgin olive oil in a saucepan. Add the onion and cook gently until soft. Add the garlic and cook for another minute. Stir in the tomatoes, season with salt and pepper, and add basil. Simmer for 20 to 30 minutes until thickened. If the sauce tastes sharp, add a small pinch of sugar.

4. **Layer the parmigiana**  
   Heat the oven to 180°C/350°F. Spoon a little tomato sauce into the bottom of a baking dish. Add a layer of aubergine, then more sauce, mozzarella, Parmesan and basil. Repeat the layers, finishing with tomato sauce, mozzarella and a generous covering of Parmesan.

5. **Bake**  
   Bake for 30 to 40 minutes, until bubbling and golden on top. Let it rest for at least 10 minutes before serving.

6. **Serve**  
   Finish with fresh basil and a drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil. Serve with a green salad, crusty bread and, ideally, enough time to sit around the table.

# Frankie Dettori’s Favorite Vegetarian Childhood Dish: Parmigiana di Melanzane

**By Food Desk | Recipe Feature**

Italian racing legend **Frankie Dettori** is best known for flying dismounts, Royal Ascot triumphs and a career that made him one of the most recognizable jockeys in the world. But away from the track, Dettori has long been associated with another Italian passion: food.

Born in Milan, Dettori grew up with the kind of home cooking that defines many Italian childhoods — simple ingredients, bold flavor and family-style dishes made to share. One classic vegetarian comfort dish closely tied to that tradition is **Parmigiana di Melanzane**, or eggplant parmigiana: layers of fried or roasted eggplant, tomato sauce, basil, mozzarella and Parmesan baked until bubbling.

Dettori has also put his name to the restaurant world. In the 2000s, he was linked with **Frankie’s Italian Bar & Grill**, a casual Italian restaurant concept created with chef **Marco Pierre White**, which expanded to several UK locations. The restaurants reflected Dettori’s public love of Italian food — generous plates, familiar classics and a lively dining-room atmosphere.

Below is a full recipe for **Parmigiana di Melanzane**, the kind of vegetarian dish that feels right at home in an Italian family kitchen.

---

## Parmigiana di Melanzane  
### Italian Eggplant Parmigiana

**Serves:** 4 to 6  
**Prep time:** 35 minutes  
**Cook time:** 50 minutes  
**Total time:** About 1 hour 25 minutes

---

## Ingredients

### For the eggplant
- 3 large eggplants/aubergines  
- 2 teaspoons salt, for drawing out moisture  
- 4 to 6 tablespoons olive oil, plus extra as needed  
- Plain flour, for dusting, optional if frying  
- Vegetable oil, for frying, optional  

### For the tomato sauce
- 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil  
- 1 small onion, finely chopped  
- 2 garlic cloves, finely sliced or minced  
- 2 x 400g cans chopped tomatoes or crushed tomatoes  
- 1 teaspoon sugar, optional  
- Salt and black pepper, to taste  
- A handful of fresh basil leaves, torn  

### For layering
- 250g mozzarella, sliced or torn  
- 75g Parmesan cheese, finely grated  
- A few extra basil leaves  
- Olive oil, for drizzling  

---

## Instructions

### 1. Prepare the eggplant  
Slice the eggplants lengthwise into pieces about ½ cm thick.

Lay the slices in a colander, sprinkling lightly with salt as you layer them. Leave for 25 to 30 minutes. This helps draw out excess moisture and any bitterness.

Rinse briefly, then pat the slices very dry with kitchen paper or a clean towel.

---

### 2. Cook the eggplant  
You can either roast or fry the eggplant.

**For a lighter version:**  
Heat the oven to **200°C / 180°C fan / 400°F**. Arrange the eggplant slices on baking trays, brush both sides with olive oil and roast for about **20 to 25 minutes**, turning once, until soft and lightly golden.

**For a more traditional version:**  
Dust the eggplant slices very lightly with flour. Heat vegetable oil in a frying pan and fry the slices in batches until golden on both sides. Drain on kitchen paper.

---

### 3. Make the tomato sauce  
Heat the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for **6 to 8 minutes**, until soft and translucent.

Add the garlic and cook for another minute, making sure it does not burn.

Pour in the tomatoes. Season with salt and black pepper. Add a small pinch of sugar if the tomatoes taste sharp.

Simmer uncovered for **20 to 25 minutes**, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens. Stir in the torn basil at the end.

---

### 4. Assemble the parmigiana  
Reduce the oven temperature to **180°C / 160°C fan / 350°F**.

Spoon a thin layer of tomato sauce into the bottom of a baking dish.

Add a layer of eggplant slices, followed by more tomato sauce, a few pieces of mozzarella, a sprinkle of Parmesan and a few basil leaves.

Repeat the layers until all the ingredients are used, finishing with tomato sauce, mozzarella and a generous topping of Parmesan.

Drizzle lightly with olive oil.

---

### 5. Bake  
Bake for **30 to 35 minutes**, or until the top is golden and bubbling.

Let the dish rest for **10 to 15 minutes** before serving. This helps the layers set and makes it easier to slice.

---

## Serving Suggestion

Serve **Parmigiana di Melanzane** warm rather than piping hot, with a crisp green salad and crusty bread. It also works beautifully as part of a larger Italian spread alongside roasted peppers, olives and a simple pasta.

---

## Cook’s Notes

- For the best flavor, use ripe canned Italian tomatoes or passata.  
- Letting the dish rest is essential; parmigiana tastes even better after the flavors settle.  
- Leftovers keep well in the fridge for up to three days and can be reheated in the oven.  
- For a richer version, add a layer of provolone or scamorza along with the mozzarella.

---

## Original Travel/Food Segment Script  
**Title: “Frankie Dettori’s Italian Table”**

**HOST:**  
When you think of Frankie Dettori, you might picture the famous flying dismount, the roar of the racecourse, and one of the most recognizable figures in international horse racing. But away from the track, Dettori’s heart has long been tied to another great Italian tradition: food.

For Frankie, restaurants have been more than business ventures. They’ve been a way to share the flavors he grew up with — generous plates, bold sauces, family-style cooking, and the kind of meals that turn an ordinary evening into a celebration. His approach to Italian food reflects the same energy he brought to racing: lively, warm, expressive, and rooted in family.

**HOST:**  
Italian cooking, at its best, is not about fuss. It’s about ingredients, patience, and memory. Tomatoes simmered until sweet. Basil torn by hand. Olive oil used with confidence. And dishes that arrive at the table bubbling hot, ready to be shared.

One such classic is **aubergine parmigiana** — or *melanzane alla parmigiana*. It’s a dish of layered aubergines, tomato sauce, cheese, and basil, baked until golden and melting. It’s rustic, comforting, and ideal for feeding a crowd.

**HOST:**  
Today, we’re making a family-sized version: rich but balanced, hearty but not heavy, and perfect for eight people around the table.

---

# Aubergine Parmigiana  
**Serves:** 8  
**Style:** Italian family-style baked dish  
**Total time:** About 1 hour 45 minutes

## Ingredients

### For the aubergines
- 5 large aubergines/eggplants  
- 3–4 tbsp olive oil, plus extra for brushing  
- Salt, to taste  
- Black pepper, to taste  

### For the tomato sauce
- 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil  
- 1 large onion, finely chopped  
- 4 garlic cloves, finely sliced or minced  
- 2 x 400 g tins chopped tomatoes  
- 500 ml passata  
- 1 tbsp tomato purée  
- 1 tsp dried oregano  
- 1 small pinch chilli flakes, optional  
- 1 tsp sugar, optional, depending on tomato acidity  
- Salt and black pepper  
- A large handful of fresh basil leaves  

### For layering
- 300 g mozzarella, drained and torn or sliced  
- 150 g Parmesan or Grana Padano, finely grated  
- 150 g provolone or scamorza, grated or thinly sliced, optional  
- Fresh basil leaves  
- Olive oil, for finishing  

---

## Method

### 1. Prepare the aubergines  
Trim the aubergines and slice them lengthways into pieces about 1 cm thick.

Lay them on trays or a large board and sprinkle lightly with salt. Leave for 20–30 minutes. This helps draw out moisture and improves the texture.

Pat the slices dry with kitchen paper.

### 2. Cook the aubergines  
Preheat the oven to **220°C / 200°C fan / 425°F**.

Brush the aubergine slices lightly with olive oil on both sides and arrange them on baking trays. Season with black pepper.

Roast for about **20–25 minutes**, turning once, until softened and lightly golden. You may need to do this in batches.

Alternatively, you can grill or pan-fry the slices, but roasting is easier when cooking for eight.

### 3. Make the tomato sauce  
While the aubergines cook, heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.

Add the onion and cook for **8–10 minutes**, until soft and translucent. Add the garlic and cook for another minute, making sure it does not burn.

Stir in the tomato purée, then add the chopped tomatoes and passata. Add oregano, chilli flakes if using, and a little salt and pepper.

Simmer uncovered for **25–30 minutes**, stirring occasionally, until thickened and rich. If the sauce tastes too sharp, add a small pinch of sugar.

Tear in the basil at the end.

### 4. Assemble the parmigiana  
Reduce the oven temperature to **190°C / 170°C fan / 375°F**.

Spoon a little tomato sauce into the base of a large baking dish.

Add a layer of roasted aubergine slices, followed by more tomato sauce, mozzarella, grated Parmesan, and a few basil leaves.

Repeat the layers until all the ingredients are used, finishing with tomato sauce, mozzarella, Parmesan, and a drizzle of olive oil.

### 5. Bake  
Bake for **35–40 minutes**, until bubbling, golden, and slightly crisp at the edges.

If the top needs more color, place it under the grill/broiler for 2–3 minutes at the end.

### 6. Rest before serving  
Let the parmigiana rest for at least **15 minutes** before cutting. This helps the layers settle and makes it easier to serve.

---

## Serving Suggestions

Serve with:

- A green salad with lemon and olive oil  
- Crusty bread or focaccia  
- Roasted peppers or marinated artichokes  
- A simple pasta course, if serving as part of a larger Italian meal  

This dish is also excellent made ahead. In fact, the flavor often improves after a few hours, or even overnight.

# A taste of Italy: Frankie Dettori, Marco Pierre White and a classic Aubergine Parmigiana

When champion jockey **Frankie Dettori** turned his attention from the racecourse to the restaurant floor, he did so with the same flair that made him one of the most recognizable figures in British sport. His partnership with celebrated chef **Marco Pierre White** brought Italian comfort food into a smart-casual dining setting, combining Dettori’s heritage and personality with White’s culinary pedigree.

Their restaurant venture, **Frankie’s Italian Bar & Grill**, became associated with several UK locations over the years, including **London**, **Chiswick**, **Knightsbridge**, **Selfridges in London**, and sites such as **Birmingham**, **Brighton**, **Cambridge**, **Dublin**, and **Abu Dhabi** at various points in the brand’s history. The concept leaned into generous Italian dishes: pasta, pizza, grilled meats and homestyle classics.

Among the dishes most closely tied to Italian home cooking is **Aubergine Parmigiana** — layers of tender aubergine, tomato sauce, basil and cheese, baked until bubbling. It is rustic, comforting and ideal as a vegetarian main course or as part of a larger Italian meal.

## Aubergine Parmigiana

### Serves  
4 as a main course, or 6 as a side dish

### Ingredients

#### For the aubergines
- 3 large aubergines  
- Salt, for drawing out moisture  
- 4–6 tablespoons olive oil, plus extra as needed  
- Freshly ground black pepper  

#### For the tomato sauce
- 2 tablespoons olive oil  
- 1 small onion, finely chopped  
- 2 garlic cloves, finely sliced or minced  
- 2 x 400g cans chopped tomatoes  
- 1 tablespoon tomato purée  
- 1 teaspoon sugar, optional  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper  
- A handful of fresh basil leaves, torn  

#### For assembling
- 200g mozzarella, sliced or torn  
- 75g Parmesan cheese, freshly grated  
- A few extra basil leaves  
- Olive oil, for drizzling  

## Method

### 1. Prepare the aubergines  
Slice the aubergines lengthways into pieces about 1cm thick. Lay them in a colander or on a tray and sprinkle lightly with salt. Leave for 20–30 minutes to draw out excess moisture and any bitterness.

Rinse briefly if heavily salted, then pat dry thoroughly with kitchen paper.

### 2. Cook the aubergines  
Heat a large frying pan or griddle pan over medium-high heat. Brush the aubergine slices with olive oil and cook in batches for 2–3 minutes on each side, until golden and softened. Season lightly with black pepper.

Alternatively, arrange the slices on baking trays, brush with olive oil and roast at 200°C/180°C fan/400°F for about 20–25 minutes, turning once, until tender and lightly browned.

### 3. Make the tomato sauce  
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 6–8 minutes, until soft but not browned. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute more.

Stir in the chopped tomatoes and tomato purée. Add sugar if the tomatoes taste sharp. Season with salt and pepper, then simmer uncovered for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened. Stir in the torn basil at the end.

### 4. Assemble the dish  
Preheat the oven to 190°C/170°C fan/375°F.

Spoon a little tomato sauce into the base of a medium baking dish. Add a layer of aubergine slices, followed by more tomato sauce, some mozzarella and a scattering of Parmesan. Repeat the layers until all the ingredients are used, finishing with tomato sauce, mozzarella and a generous layer of Parmesan.

Drizzle lightly with olive oil.

### 5. Bake  
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until the top is golden and bubbling and the sauce is visibly thick around the edges.

### 6. Rest and serve  
Leave the parmigiana to rest for 10 minutes before serving. Finish with a few fresh basil leaves.

Serve warm with a green salad, crusty bread or as part of an Italian-style spread.

## Cook’s notes

- For a richer version, fry the aubergine slices in olive oil rather than grilling or roasting them.  
- The dish can be made a day ahead and reheated; the flavors often improve overnight.  
- Smoked mozzarella or scamorza can add depth, while a little dried oregano in the sauce gives a more southern Italian flavor.

50–60 minutes

4–6
